milestone.title: raul Settings 2.0 — typed config schema, inline editors, description card with defaults

intent.outcome: The raul Settings lane shows all 46 settings in a framed list with a framed description card under it. Each setting displays Type / Default / Value / Description. Booleans toggle in place, choices cycle in place, strings / paths / integers edit in-row with a caret, keybinds use a typed-string editor with KeyCombo::parse validation. The centered popup modal is gone for the common case. Settings 2.0 unblocks a more discoverable, typed, modern configuration surface for raul.

problem.description: The current Settings lane (M140 / M168) has a flat `key = value` list, an unanchored 3-row prose block at the top, and a centered popup modal for every edit. The renderer has no schema — types, defaults, and allowed values are implicit in the JSON config; the help text in `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings/help.rs` is the only source of per-key prose and has drifted from the typed `Keybinds::default()` impl on ~12 of 28 keybinds. The user has no separation between 'what the key does' and 'what value is set right now' on the same screen. The modal-heavy flow breaks the visual continuity with the rest of the TUI (milestone list, backlog list, milestone detail), which all use the same bordered-block-with-accent-title vocabulary.

in_scope: New `mp config schema` subcommand that emits a JSON document with one entry per recognized config key (46 keys across ui, workflow, git, next, agent, keybinds). Each entry: {key, type, default, allowed?, description}. `type` is one of `bool | choice | string | integer | path | keybind`. `allowed` is present only for `choice` (e.g. ui.theme allowed: [mocha, latte, frappe, macchiato, dracula]). `description` is the user-facing one-liner from the key_descriptions block below. Deterministic ordering (sorted by key, then section).

New `SettingsSchema` data structure in `crates/raul/src/tui/mode.rs` (or a new `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings/schema.rs`) that holds the per-key metadata. `SettingsState` reads the schema once on lane open and caches it. No re-fetch on every redraw.

Reworked `render_settings_lane` in `crates/raul/src/tui/render/overlays.rs`:
  - Bordered list at the top, with section headers (ui, workflow, git, next, agent, keybinds) styled like the milestone list's indent column. Cursor on a Key row (REVERSED).
  - Framed description card UNDER the list (not above). Border in accent color. Title is the focused key. Body shows `Type / Default / Value / Description` as a BOLD-label grid, plus a hint footer (e.g. 'Enter: edit · ←/→: cycle · s: save · Esc: back to list').
  - Replaces the current 3-row un-bordered prose block and the centered popup for the common case.
  - The keybind capture modal (if shipped in a follow-up) is the only remaining modal; everything else edits inline.

Per-type inline editors, all on the row, all in the same visual block:
  - `bool`: Space toggles in place. No editor. The description card hint changes to 'Space: toggle · s: save · Esc: back'.
  - `choice`: ← / → cycles through `allowed` values. The value cell renders `‹ current ›  (was previous)` while cycling. No editor. Hint: '←/→: cycle · s: save · Esc: revert'.
  - `string` / `path` / `integer`: Enter drops the value cell into a caret-edit state, in-row. Backspace deletes; arrow keys move; Enter commits; Esc reverts. Invalid values (e.g. integer parse failure) show a red error line in the description card area, Enter retries, Esc reverts.
  - `keybind`: typed-string editor with `KeyCombo::parse` validation. Same in-row caret as strings. Invalid combos (e.g. 'asdf') show the parse error in the description card area, Enter retries, Esc reverts. Valid combos commit on Enter.

Bake the 46 per-key descriptions from the planning-session sign-off into the schema (see `key_descriptions` below). Descriptions are user-facing: no `crates/...` pointers, no internal milestone IDs, no lesson codes. Defaults in the description card come from the typed `Default` impls in `crates/mp/src/config.rs` and `crates/raul/src/tui/keybinds.rs`; no echo in the prose.

Tests: per-type editor unit tests (Bool toggle, Choice cycle, String/Path/Integer commit + revert, Keybind typed-string commit + invalid-retry), a TUI snapshot test for the framed list + framed description card layout, a golden `mp config schema` fixture under `tests/fixtures/golden/`, a CLI scenario test that asserts the schema output is deterministic and includes all 46 keys. Consumer-surface lint clean (no internal IDs leak into descriptions or the schema JSON).
Update the `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings/help.rs` file: delete it (or replace with a thin re-export from the new schema doc) once M201 ships. Until then, it is no longer read by the renderer.

out_of_scope: Keybind capture mode (press-the-combo modal). v1 ships the typed-string editor; capture mode is a polish follow-up. The user explicitly chose typed-string for v1 in the planning session.
Search / filter on the settings list. Operators with 46 rows don't need it; can be added later if the list grows.
Per-user (vs per-project) preference scoping. Same as the rest of the config: project-level. Per-user would touch the config read path and is a separate change.
Change to the persisted config format. The TOML shape stays the same; the schema is read-only metadata for the TUI.
Change to `mp config get / set / unset` semantics. Existing CLI behavior is preserved (AC-06).
New config keys. The 46 settings are the full set; no additions in this milestone.
Theme / palette additions. `ui.theme` accepts the existing 5 themes (mocha, latte, frappe, macchiato, dracula); no new palette work.
A migration / shim for users whose config has drifted help-text defaults. Existing overrides win, just like M200.

Markdown rendering inside the description card. Per the planning session, structured BOLD-label fields are sufficient; markdown rendering is reserved for longer-form prose (e.g. milestone detail) and adds no value here.

Each type's inline editor works without opening a modal:

acceptance_criteria.description: When `mp config schema` is unavailable (older mp, unknown subcommand), the Settings lane shows a clear error: the schema command is missing and the operator should upgrade mp (include `mp --version` in the hint). The error replaces the framed list — no half-rendered state.

design_decisions.choice: New `mp config schema` subcommand (not `mp config show --schema` flag).
design_decisions.rationale: The schema is a different shape than `config show` (which is the merged config object). A separate subcommand is the cleanest surface for a typed, machine-readable contract. The agent (and any future tooling) reads schema once and caches. The TUI consumes the same JSON.

Matches the milestone list + milestone detail pattern: the list is the index, the detail card is the focus. Above-the-list would compete with the list for the same first-glance eye path. Below matches what the user has been reading in the planning mockup.

Smallest path to a single cohesive milestone. Capture mode (press-the-combo) is the right UX but adds a day of code+test and keeps one modal in the surface. The user picked typed-string for v1 in the planning session; capture mode is a polish follow-up.

design_decisions.choice: Typed Default impls in crates/mp/src/config.rs for non-keybind keys. Keybind defaults live in a KEYBIND_DEFAULTS table in crates/mp/src/config_docs.rs, duplicated from raul Keybinds::default() (mp must not depend on raul — same pattern as KEYBIND_ACTIONS). A unit test pins the two tables stay in lockstep. No echo of defaults in the prose.
design_decisions.rationale: crates/mp/src/config.rs already documents that mp cannot depend on raul (UI_THEMES / KEYBIND_ACTIONS are duplicated deliberately). Wiring Keybinds::default() into mp config schema would add a forbidden crate edge. Duplicating the default chords next to the descriptions keeps a single compile unit and a lockstep test.

design_decisions.area: Where the 46 descriptions live in source
design_decisions.choice: A const array in `crates/mp/src/config_docs.rs` (new file), keyed by the dotted key, with `{type, default, allowed?, description}` per entry. `mp config schema` reads it and merges with the typed default-impl fallback (typed wins on conflict, so the description array can omit `default` and still be correct).
design_decisions.rationale: Descriptions are user-facing prose; they belong in `mp` (the consumer-facing crate) not `raul` (the TUI). A new file keeps the schema-source-of-truth together. The typed `Default` impls remain the runtime default; the description array is the prose. The schema command merges them at emit time.

design_decisions.choice: Read once on lane open and cache in `SettingsState`. No re-fetch on redraw; no re-fetch on key change.
design_decisions.rationale: Schema is static for the lifetime of a project (no key added/removed at runtime). Caching is the right call for TUI redraw performance. A future 'reload schema' command (out of scope) is the path for picking up new keys after `mp` upgrades.

design_decisions.choice: Three states per row: `idle` (default), `editing` (caret in value cell), `invalid` (editing + parse error). The same `SettingsFocus` enum that already exists is extended; no new mode is added.
design_decisions.rationale: The current `SettingsFocus::Editing` flag is the only mode-level signal needed. The per-type editor (Bool / Choice / String / Path / Integer / Keybind) lives on the row's `SettingsEdit` struct. One mode signal, six type-specific editors — keeps the dispatch flat.

design_decisions.choice: Bordered blocks with accent border (description card) and neutral border (list). Same `Borders::ALL` + title pattern used by `render_backlog_detail` and the milestone detail card. `REVERSED` cursor for the focused row. No new color roles in the palette.
design_decisions.rationale: No new visual vocabulary. The user explicitly asked for continuity with the rest of the TUI; this is the same `Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL).title(...)` + accent-border treatment the milestone list uses.

design_decisions.choice: Detect the missing subcommand (`unknown subcommand` / non-zero from `mp config schema`). Show an error that names `mp config schema` and tells the operator to upgrade mp, including `mp --version` in the hint. Do not hard-code a version number like 0.X.Y in the shipped string.
design_decisions.rationale: A placeholder version in the AC would ship literally. Capability detection (does the subcommand exist?) is more honest than a version floor the runner cannot know at spec time.

design_decisions.choice: The schema output includes a top-level `$schema_version: "1.0"` (semver string) field. Additive changes (new optional fields, new types, new keys) bump minor; breaking changes (renamed fields, removed fields, changed semantics) bump major. Consumers (raul, future tooling) can use the version to negotiate capability without re-reading the schema on every release.
design_decisions.rationale: The schema is now a stable contract — raul parses it on lane open, and any future agent / IDE consumer will too. Without a version field, every change is a silent breaking change for any strict consumer. The semver discipline matches the rest of the projects interfaces (the `mp` CLI uses semver, the JSON config format is a separate compat contract).

design_decisions.choice: 45 keys. Omit keybinds.focus_content even if the drafting JSON in in_scope still lists it (that blob was captured before M200 dropped the config surface).
design_decisions.rationale: M200 removes focus_content from SETTINGS_KEYS and KEYBIND_ACTIONS. Baking it into the schema would resurrect a key the deconflict just deleted.

open_questions.question: Should `mp config schema` be a subcommand (recommended) or a `--schema` flag on `mp config show`?
open_questions.answer: New subcommand. The schema is a different shape than 'config show' (which is the merged config object), and any future tooling (agents, validation harnesses, IDE integrations) benefits from a stable, machine-readable contract at a predictable path. 'mp config show --schema' would also work but mixes two output shapes in one subcommand. The schema subcommand wins on clarity.

open_questions.question: Where exactly in `crates/mp/src/` do the 46 descriptions live? New file `config_docs.rs` (recommended) or an extension of `crates/mp/src/config.rs`?
open_questions.answer: New file 'crates/mp/src/config_docs.rs'. The descriptions are user-facing prose; they belong in 'mp' (the consumer-facing crate) and are large enough (46 entries) to justify a dedicated file. The typed 'Default' impls in 'config.rs' remain the runtime default; 'config_docs.rs' is the prose source. The 'mp config schema' command merges them at emit time (typed wins on conflict).

open_questions.question: When the inline keybind editor gets an invalid combo, where exactly does the error render — under the row, in the description card, or both?
open_questions.answer: Description card. The error line renders in the description card's hint footer area, replacing the per-type hint temporarily. The row itself stays in the 'editing' state with the caret in the value cell. This keeps the layout stable (the description card never grows a new region; it just swaps its hint for an error) and matches the rest of the TUI's pattern of 'errors live in the same place every time'.

open_questions.question: For the typed-string keybind editor, do we accept any user-typed string that `KeyCombo::parse` can interpret (e.g. `Ctrl+S`, `+`, bare `Enter`) or do we restrict to a documented subset?
open_questions.answer: Accept any user-typed string that 'KeyCombo::parse' can interpret, including multi-modifier combos like 'Ctrl+Shift+S'. We do not restrict to a documented subset; the typed impl in 'crates/raul/src/tui/key_combo.rs' is the authoritative grammar and the typed-string editor surfaces its parse errors verbatim. Documented key names like 'Enter', 'Esc', 'Up', 'PageUp', 'BackTab', 'Tab' are supported; the description card hint for keybind rows shows 'e.g. Ctrl+R, Enter, PageUp' as a prompt.

open_questions.question: When the user toggles a Bool or cycles a Choice, is the change staged (committed on `s`) or live (committed immediately, with no staging)?
open_questions.answer: Staged. Bool toggles and Choice cycles record into 'state.staged_edits' immediately (so the value cell updates visually), but the on-disk config only changes when the user presses 's' to save. The Esc revert path restores the pre-edit value. This matches the existing 's' saves the staged edits pattern in 'modes/settings.rs' and avoids surprise writes from a key press.

Include a KEYBIND_DEFAULTS table duplicating raul Keybinds::default() chords — mp must not depend on raul.

steps.action: Rework `render_settings_lane` in `crates/raul/src/tui/render/overlays.rs`. (1) Replace the flat `key = value` List with a bordered block at the top: section headers (ui, workflow, git, next, agent, keybinds) styled like the milestone list indent column; Key rows with the type badge in a small column; value cell shows the current value. (2) Below the list, add a framed description card with the focused key name in the title (accent border); body is a BOLD-label `Type / Default / Value / Description` grid; footer is a per-type hint line.

steps.action: Bool editor. When the focused key has `type = bool` and the user presses Space, the value cell flips immediately and the change is staged in `state.staged_edits`. No editor opens. The description card hint shows `Space: toggle · s: save · Esc: back`.
steps.done_when: Bool keys toggle in place on Space; the change is staged; the value cell updates visually

steps.action: Choice editor. When the focused key has `type = choice` and the user presses Left or Right, the value cycles through `allowed` (wrapping). While cycling, the value cell renders `‹ current ›` (with a `‹` / `›` indicator). The change is staged on each press. No editor opens. The description card hint shows `←/→: cycle · s: save · Esc: revert`.
steps.done_when: Choice keys cycle on Left/Right; the value cell shows the current option; the change is staged

steps.action: String / Path / Integer editor. When the focused key has `type = string`, `path`, or `integer` and the user presses Enter, the value cell drops into a caret-edit state. Backspace deletes the char before the caret; Left/Right move the caret; Enter commits; Esc reverts. Integer keys validate parse on commit; invalid values show `not a valid integer: <input>` in the description card hint footer, Enter retries, Esc reverts. The change is staged on commit.
steps.done_when: String/Path/Integer keys edit in-row; integer validates on commit; invalid values show in the description card hint

steps.action: Keybind editor. When the focused key has `type = keybind` and the user presses Enter, the value cell drops into a caret-edit state. The user types a combo string (e.g. `Ctrl+S`, `Enter`, `PageUp`); the editor calls `KeyCombo::parse` on Enter. Valid combos commit and stage; invalid combos show the parse error in the description card hint footer, Enter retries, Esc reverts. The description card hint shows `e.g. Ctrl+R, Enter, PageUp` as a prompt.
steps.done_when: Keybind keys edit in-row; valid combos commit; invalid combos show the parse error; the typed-string editor handles every `KeyCombo::parse` case
